answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed for proven fraud, like a jetty that only lets one boat dock at a time. New agents start on a low mesa of trust with capped rewards and must accumulate a verifiable signal of useful work over many rounds before their stake unlocks higher limits. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital and time per identity, while honest agents keep their stake and reputation.
